fact_text: A candlestick plots open, high, low and close for one time frame: the body runs from open to close and the wicks show the high and low touched. A green candle closed above its open, a red candle closed below it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: Candlestick charts are the common price plot for stocks, forex, crypto and commodities, and they are read the same way on daily, weekly and other time frames.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: Technical analysis studies historic price movement to judge what the market may do next, and every element of it is based on price.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: Indicators are formulas applied to historic price data, such as a 20-day moving average, and are read alongside price action rather than instead of it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: Markets usually move in a zigzag: an impulsive move up is followed by profit taking, which causes a pullback or correction, and clean one-way trends are rare.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: An uptrend is a run of higher highs and higher lows; the trend is intact while each new low holds above the previous low.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: An uptrend turns into a downtrend when the previous low breaks, and lower lows then begin to form.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: A downtrend is a run of lower highs and lower lows; a new high that does not break the previous high is a lower high and confirms the downtrend.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: In a downtrend the trend change is first seen when the previous high breaks, which creates a new higher high and marks a change of trend.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: In a choppy uptrend, lower highs that do not break the prior high are not a warning; mark a horizontal line at the last low and watch whether the next lows break it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: Support is the floor where a falling market tends to bounce, and resistance is the ceiling where a rising market tends to stall and pull back.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: A resistance level that breaks tends to become support on the next pullback, and a support level that breaks tends to become resistance, which lets the trend continue.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: In an uptrend, after a resistance breaks, price pulls back to that level, holds it as support and resumes higher, and the same process repeats at each new resistance.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: Before trading a daily chart that is making new highs, the analyst checks the weekly chart to mark the historic support and resistance levels, since the larger levels matter more.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: On 27 May 2024 the KSE-100 daily chart showed a plain downtrend, with each new high below the previous high and each new low below the previous low.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: As of 27 May 2024 Lucky Cement was trading at a price level last seen in 2021, when it made two highs, and the analyst treated the 2021 pullback zone as the key level on the weekly chart.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: The 2021 pullback in Lucky Cement acted as resistance in November 2021, and the analyst said the same zone later acted as support and resistance, so the weekly levels matter for trading.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Technical Analysis Series for PSX Investors: Let's learn about Price Action and Support/Resistance' (YouTube, 2024-05-27)

fact_text: On the Lucky Cement daily chart as of 27 May 2024 the resistance at the last high is the level to watch; the analyst expected that a break of it would turn that resistance into support.
